headline: High: agentic-flow can modify shared state and use MCP, creating default conflict and injection pathways with PaddleOCR’s document inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest external content through shared channels; agent_b processes documents/images that can carry attacker-controlled text. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven, but uncertainty raises severity above low.
conditions: IF agent_a reads agent_b output from a shared file, pipe, or MCP message without provenance checks
IF agent_b processes untrusted documents that are later interpreted as instructions by agent_a
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all agent_b outputs before agent_a consumes them
Disable automatic instruction-following on OCR text
Route agent_b output through a human review step
Restrict MCP channels to structured data only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and secrets (Ed25519 signatures), while agent_b processes documents and images. A shared workspace or file handoff could leak sensitive material into OCR outputs or logs. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so this is an inferred medium-risk interaction.
conditions: IF agent_a writes prompts, code, or signatures into files that agent_b reads
IF agent_b uploads document contents to a remote inference/API backend during processing
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b in separate workspaces
Do not place secrets in shared directories
Mask signatures and prompts before OCR ingestion
Review outbound requests from agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can run browsers and make allowlisted network egress. Overlapping mutable actions can conflict if both operate on the same repo or workspace, though no locking mechanism is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or working directory
IF agent_a modifies git state while agent_b generates or rewrites files in that workspace
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a simple operator lock
Pause browser automation during git writes
Check git status before and after each run
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce analysis artifacts and modify repository state, and agent_b can consume documents/images that may be derived from those artifacts. If agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream OCR or document-processing results. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-generated files without validation
IF agent_a’s generated text is used as ground truth for document extraction or translation
mitigations: Require checksum or schema validation on handoff files
Insert a review step before agent_b consumes agent_a output
Keep generated artifacts separate from source documents
Log provenance for each handoff
requires-engineering: add typed interfaces between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and only allowlisted egress is documented, with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or retention mismatch in the profiles. Compliance risk is therefore limited to undocumented policy gaps rather than a known breach pathway. The evidence is sparse, so I avoid none but keep severity low.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated documents through a non-approved external API
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two agents in the operator’s environment
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Keep regulated data out of allowlisted egress paths
Document retention settings for both agents
Review vendor terms for OCR/document processing
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
